brief_item.title: LLMCompiler 自动并行化Agent函数调用
brief_item.core_conclusion: 多工具LLM Agent对每次函数调用采用串行ReAct式推理-执行，即便相互独立的调用也逐个运行，造成高时延与高成本。LLMCompiler由Planner自动识别可并行与相互依赖的调用并生成任务DAG，再由Task Fetching Unit解析依赖、Executor并行调度，以流式方式将任务从Planner即时送至Executor。
brief_item.mechanism: Planner将用户请求分解为任务并区分并行与依赖，生成优化编排（任务DAG）；Task Fetching Unit解析依赖，Executor并行派发调用；流式传输在任务生成后立即送出而非等待整计划完成。用户提供工具及可选上下文示例，Planner可泛化至开源（LLaMA、vLLM、Friendli）与闭源（OpenAI、Azure）模型。
brief_item.result: README声明在HotpotQA、Movie Recommendation、ParallelQA基准上相对ReAct基线实现时延降低、成本节省与准确率提升（README未给出具体幅度，数值需查阅ICML论文）。；仓库提供--react基线对照与--stream流式执行选项，支持OpenAI、Azure及vLLM/Friendli自托管端点。
brief_item.boundary: 来源为项目README而非ICML论文：仅定性声明收益，未给出数值幅度、置信区间或分模型明细；投机并行执行在依赖误判时的浪费与正确性风险未量化。工作负载为通用函数调用QA，非编码Agent的Read/Grep工具，迁移到代码搜索加速属推断。
brief_item.project_relevance: [判断]Agent工具链并行执行的核心参考：独立工具调用并发而非串行的经典方法，可直接用于并行化编码Agent的独立Read/Grep/Glob调用。Planner/Task-Fetching-Unit/Executor拆分与流式是降低Agent端到端时延的可复用设计模式，但仓库未评测编码Agent负载。

facts.title: LLMCompiler: An LLM Compiler for Parallel Function Calling (ICML 2024, project README)
facts.event_hint: LLM compiler that plans and executes parallel function calls for tool-using LLMs
facts.problem: Sequential ReAct-style reasoning-and-acting for each function call in multi-tool LLM agents creates high latency, high cost, and sometimes inaccurate behavior, because independently-callable functions are still executed one at a time.
facts.mechanism: LLMCompiler decomposes a user request into tasks, and a Planner automatically identifies which function calls can run in parallel versus which are interdependent, then computes an optimized orchestration (a task DAG). A Task Fetching Unit resolves dependencies and an Executor dispatches parallel calls; streaming pipes tasks from the Planner to the Executor immediately as they are generated rather than blocking until the full plan is produced. Users supply tools plus optional in-context examples; the planner generalizes across open-source (LLaMA, vLLM-served, Friendli) and closed (OpenAI GPT, Azure) models.

evidence.claim: LLMCompiler identifies which tasks can be performed in parallel and which are interdependent, orchestrating multi-function calling automatically.
evidence.source_locator: README TL;DR: 'automatically identifying which tasks can be performed in parallel and which ones are interdependent'

evidence.claim: The user specifies tools with optional in-context examples and LLMCompiler computes an optimized orchestration for the function calls.
Streaming emits tasks from the Planner to the Task Fetching Unit and Executor immediately after generation, improving latency versus blocking until all tasks are generated.
Across tasks with different parallel-calling patterns, LLMCompiler demonstrated latency speedup, cost saving, and accuracy improvement.
evidence.source_locator: README TL;DR; baseline ReAct supported via --react flag

evidence.claim: Supported benchmarks are HotpotQA, Movie Recommendation, and ParallelQA; ReAct is provided as the baseline comparator.

facts.evaluation_context: Benchmarks bundled in the repo: HotpotQA, Movie Recommendation (movie), ParallelQA. Baseline is ReAct. OpenAI GPT models used by default; custom models via vLLM and Friendli endpoints also supported; Azure endpoint supported. No specific speedup percentages, token counts, or hardware are given in the README.
facts.limitations: This is the project README, not the ICML paper; it states that speedup/cost/accuracy gains occurred but gives no numeric magnitudes, confidence intervals, or model-specific breakdowns (those require the paper). Correctness/risk of speculative parallel execution (e.g., wasted calls when dependencies are mis-predicted) is not quantified here. Workloads are general function-calling QA tasks, not coding-agent Read/Grep tools, so direct transfer to code-search acceleration is an inference.
facts.project_relevance: Core reference for the agent tool-chain parallel-execution question: it is the canonical method for running independent tool calls concurrently instead of sequentially, which is directly applicable to parallelizing a coding agent's independent Read/Grep/Glob calls. The Planner/Task-Fetching-Unit/Executor split and streaming are reusable design patterns for reducing agent end-to-end latency. Relevance to code-graph and speculative tool execution is high, though the repo does not evaluate coding-agent workloads.
source_notes: Document is the official GitHub README for SqueezeAILab/LLMCompiler (ICML 2024); primary source for the framework design and usage, but not for numeric evaluation results.
Authors per citation: Kim, Moon, Tabrizi, Lee, Mahoney, Keutzer, Gholami (arXiv 2023, ICML 2024).
Numeric latency/cost/accuracy figures are absent; consult the paper for magnitudes.
